chapter.li: LEChapter16 Verse1 In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and His robe filled the temple. VerseEnd Verse2 Seraphs gathered around Him. Each one had six wings: with two he veiled his face, and with two he covered his legs, and with two he would fly. VerseEnd Verse3 And one would call to the other, saying: Holy, holy, holy! The Lord of Hosts! The whole earth is within His view! VerseEnd Verse4 And the doorframe would shake at the sound of that voice, and clouds billowed around God’s throne. VerseEnd

Verse5 Then I said: Woe is me, I’m lost, for my lips are unclean, and I live among people whose lips are also unclean, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd Verse6 Then one of the seraphs flew to me with a live coal in his hand, which he used tongs to take from the altar. VerseEnd Verse7 And he touched my lips and declared: Hear now, this has touched 2PSI your lips, 2PSI your guilt is taken away, and 2PSI your iniquity cleaned away. VerseEnd Verse8 Then I heard the voice of the Lord asking: Whom do I send? Who will go for us? And I said: Here am I; send me. VerseEnd Verse9 And He said: Go tell the people: Listen to this message — but they won’t understand what 2PSI you tell them; and tell them to see 2PSI your message — but they’ll fail to perceive its meaning. VerseEnd Verse10 Their minds have become dull, their ears plugged, and their eyes closed, otherwise they would see with their eyes, hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and be healed. VerseEnd Verse11 Then I asked: Lord, how long will they remain like this? And He said: Until their cities have been destroyed and left desolate, and their houses abandoned, and the land deserted, VerseEnd Verse12 until the Lord has driven everyone far away, and there are many abandoned places throughout the land. VerseEnd Verse13 But a tithe of the people will remain and will be burned. Like a linden tree or oak tree, leaving a stump with living roots although cut down, likewise a holy remnant to be restored still survives in the residue. VerseEnd

LEChapter17 Verse1 When Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, king Rezin of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up to fight against Jerusalem, but they couldn’t defeat it. VerseEnd Verse2 When the report reached the house of David that Syria is allied with Ephraim, they all panicked and trembled like the trees of the forest wave in the wind. VerseEnd

Verse3 Then the Lord directed Isaiah: Go out with 2PSI your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the channel of the upper pool on the road to the Laundry Field. VerseEnd Verse4 Tell him: Relax and be quiet; don’t be afraid of these two smoldering embers of firewood because of the anger of Rezin of Syria and Remaliah’s son. VerseEnd Verse5 Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah’s son have plotted 2PSI your defeat, saying: VerseEnd Verse6 Let’s invade Judah, tear it apart, and divide it up between us, and put the son of Tabeal over it as the king. VerseEnd Verse7 The Lord God says: It won’t happen, I won’t let it take place. VerseEnd Verse8 For the center of Syria is Damascus, and the king of Damascus is Rezin. And within 65 years Ephraim will be shattered, no longer identifiable. VerseEnd Verse9 The center of Ephraim is Samaria, and the king of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If 2PP you won’t stand faithful, 2PP you won’t stand at all. VerseEnd

Verse10 The Lord invited Ahaz to: VerseEnd Verse11 Ask the Lord 2PSI your God for a sign; anything from the deepest to the highest place. VerseEnd Verse12 But Ahaz said: I won’t ask, nor will I test the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 Then Isaiah said: Listen now, 2PP you house of David: Is it not enough 2PP you try the patience of men? Now 2PP you want to try God’s patience also? VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore the Lord Himself will give 2PP you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son and will call Him Immanuel. VerseEnd Verse15 By the time He learns to reject the bad and choose the good, people will be eating butter and honey. VerseEnd Verse16 Before the lad learns to reject evil and choose good, the land of these two kings will be wasted. VerseEnd Verse17 The Lord will bring upon 2PSI you and 2PSI your people and 2PSI your father’s house the worst days since Ephraim broke away from Judah — that king of Assyria. VerseEnd Verse18 In that day the Lord will whistle for flies from the Nile delta in Egypt, and for bees from the land of Assyria. VerseEnd Verse19 They’ll come and land in the rugged valleys, and in the cracks of the rocks, and on thorn bushes, and beside 2PSI your ponds. VerseEnd Verse20 On the same day the Lord will hire the king of Assyria like a razor to shave 2PSI your head, legs, and beard. VerseEnd

Verse21 And in that day, a man will raise a young cow and two sheep. VerseEnd Verse22 And because of the abundance of milk they produce, he’ll have butter. Everyone remaining in the land will have butter and honey. VerseEnd Verse23 And at that time, every place where there were 1,000 grapevines worth 1,000 silver coins, there will only be weeds and thorns left. VerseEnd Verse24 Hunters will go there with bows and arrows because the land is covered with weeds and thorns. VerseEnd Verse25 As for the once plowed and cultivated hills, 2PSI you’ll no longer go there to see weeds and thorns, since only cattle will graze and only sheep will roam on these places. VerseEnd

LEChapter18 Verse1 The Lord said to me: Take a large scroll and write on it with a pen: For Maher-shalal-hash-baz. VerseEnd Verse2 Call two reliable witnesses, Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah, to witness it. VerseEnd Verse3 I then impregnated the prophetess, and she gave birth to a son. The Lord told me: Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz. VerseEnd Verse4 Before the child learns to call, Father and Mother, the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria. VerseEnd

Verse5 The Lord spoke to me again, saying: VerseEnd Verse6 Because this people are ungrateful for the gentle waters of Shiloah, and admire Rezin and Remaliah’s son, VerseEnd Verse7 know this, the Lord will bring to them a flood of violent water from the Euphrates, indeed, the king of Assyria and his army. He’ll flood over the riverbanks, VerseEnd Verse8 like a flash flood upon Judah, reaching up to the neck. Surely the wings of Immanuel will stretch out as wide as the land. VerseEnd Verse9 Even if 2PP you people gather together people, 2PP you’ll too be broken into pieces. Listen, those who are in distant lands: Even if 2PP you prepare for battle, 2PP you’ll be broken into pieces; 2PP you may prepare for battle, but 2PP you’ll be broken in pieces! VerseEnd Verse10 Though 2PP you prepare 2PP your battle strategy, it will be defeated; though 2PP you make 2PP your plans, they won’t stand, because God is with us. VerseEnd

Verse11 The Lord said to me, taking me by the hand, and telling me to not walk in the path this people follow, saying: VerseEnd Verse12 Don’t say: A conspiracy! to everything this people says is a conspiracy; don’t be afraid of what they fear. VerseEnd Verse13 Only the Lord of Hosts is to be regarded as holy, and He alone inspires awe. VerseEnd Verse14 He can make things holy, but for the people of Jerusalem, He’ll be a stumbling stone and a rock that trips both houses of Israel, and a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse15 Many of them will stumble, fall down, and be injured, and be caught and taken captive. VerseEnd

Verse16 Deliver the testimony, seal up the law among My disciples. VerseEnd Verse17 I’ll wait for the Lord who hides His face from the house of Jacob, and I’ll put my trust in Him. VerseEnd Verse18 Here am I and the children the Lord has given me. We are signs and symbols in Israel from the Lord of Hosts, who lives on Mount Zion. VerseEnd Verse19 When people advise 2PP you to ask gurus and false spirits that whisper and moan — shouldn’t people instead ask God? Why ask the dead for advice for the living? VerseEnd Verse20 Shouldn’t people look for direction from God’s law and His warning testimony? And if anyone speaks contrary to this word, it’s because there’s no light in them. VerseEnd Verse21 And they’ll wander lost, wretched, and hungry; and when they’re hungry, they’ll become angry, look up to heaven and curse their King and their God. VerseEnd Verse22 And they’ll look at the earth and see trouble and darkness, gloom and fear, and won’t see the dawn. VerseEnd

LEChapter19 Verse1 Nevertheless, the gloom will depart from those who were in distress. In the past, He humbled the land of Zebulun, and the land of Naphtali, but in the future, He’ll honor Galilee by the Way of the Sea, on the other side of the Jordan. VerseEnd Verse2 The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; those living in the land of deep darkness have had the light dawn on them. VerseEnd Verse3 2PSI You’ve enlarged that nation and given it great joy; they rejoice before 2PSI You like the harvest celebration, and like warriors are happy when dividing their loot. VerseEnd Verse4 Because 2PSI You’ve broken their chains, and the bar across their shoulders, the club used by their oppressor, VerseEnd Verse5 every warrior’s boot worn in battle and all the bloodstained clothes will become fuel for the fire. VerseEnd Verse6 For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulder. And His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, the Mighty God, the Everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace. VerseEnd Verse7 His government and peace will endlessly increase, He’ll sit on the throne of David and reign over His kingdom, establishing and upholding it with righteousness and with justice from that time continuing forever. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will cause this to happen. VerseEnd

Verse8 The Lord sent a message condemning Jacob, and it will fall upon Israel. VerseEnd Verse9 Everyone will know it — Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria — who say in their pride and arrogance: VerseEnd Verse10 The bricks are fallen down, but we’ll rebuild with cut stones; the sycamores are cut down, but we’ll replace them with cedars. VerseEnd Verse11 So the Lord allowed the enemies of Rezin to come against him, and his enemies joined together — VerseEnd Verse12 the Syrians from the east and the Philistines from the west — and they’ll swallow up Israel. Despite this His anger remains, and His control over everything remains intact. VerseEnd

Verse13 But His people haven’t returned to Him who punished them; they reject the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore the Lord cut off the head and tail from Israel, palm branch and reed, in a single day. VerseEnd Verse15 The leaders and teachers are the head, and the lying prophets are the tail. VerseEnd Verse16 The guides of this people mislead them, and those who follow stumble in the dark. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore the Lord will have no sympathy for their young men, nor pity the orphans and widows; for every one of them is a hypocrite and ungodly, and every mouth speaks foolishness. Despite this His anger remains, and His control over everything remains intact. VerseEnd

Verse18 Wickedness burns like a fire destroying weeds and thorns, and sets ablaze the forests, rolling forward like a pillar of smoke. VerseEnd Verse19 It’s the wrath of the Lord of Hosts that scorches the land and the people become fuel for the fire; they won’t spare one another. VerseEnd Verse20 On the right hand they gobble up but remain hungry, on the left they eat but are never satisfied. They’ll eat their own families — VerseEnd Verse21 Ephraim eating Manasseh’s, and Manasseh eating Ephraim’s — and together they eat Judah’s. Nevertheless, His anger remains, and His control over everything remains intact. VerseEnd

LEChapter20 Verse1 Woe to those who make unjust laws, and to those who issue oppressive orders, VerseEnd Verse2 subverting the rights of the poor, denying justice and imposing tyranny, victimizing widows and orphans. VerseEnd Verse3 What will 2PP you do on the day of judgment, when disaster comes from far away? Where will 2PP you run for help? Where will 2PP you hide 2PP your riches? VerseEnd Verse4 2PP You’ll have no choice but to cower among the prisoners or be killed with the others. Despite this His anger remains, and His control over everything remains intact. VerseEnd

Verse5 But the Assyrians are only the club I use to impose My discipline. VerseEnd Verse6 I send them against a godless nation, and against the people who have angered Me, to loot and plunder, and trample over them like mud in the streets. VerseEnd Verse7 But this isn’t what the Assyrians intend, not at all what they have in mind. They intend to destroy and defeat many nations. VerseEnd Verse8 Their king tells himself: Aren’t my commanders all kings? VerseEnd Verse9 Hasn’t Calno fallen just like Carchemish? Isn’t Hamath just like Arpad? Isn’t Samaria just like Damascus? VerseEnd Verse10 My hand has conquered the kingdoms of the idols, kingdoms whose idols are better than those of Jerusalem and Samaria. VerseEnd Verse11 Should I not deal with Jerusalem and her idols as I dealt with Samaria and her idols? VerseEnd

Verse12 But when the Lord has finished all His discipline of Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He’ll then punish the prideful king of Assyria for his arrogance. VerseEnd Verse13 For he says it’s his strong hand and his wisdom that accomplished this, because he claims understanding. He says he’s the one that changed national boundaries and pilfered their wealth, like a great hero, saying: VerseEnd Verse14 I’ve taken the wealth of other countries like reaching 2PG your hand into a nest to gather eggs, and they didn’t flap a wing or cluck when I took it all. VerseEnd Verse15 Is the ax greater than the one who swings it? Does the saw brag it cuts wood without the one using it? As if a club could control the one holding it, or a staff steer the person as if it weren’t mere wood. VerseEnd Verse16 Therefore, the Lord, the Lord of Hosts will inflict disease on his army; and under his pomposity a fire will be kindled. VerseEnd Verse17 The Light of Israel will be that fire, and Israel’s Holy One the flame, and in a single day it will turn his weeds and thorns to ash VerseEnd Verse18 and burn up his splendid forest and fertile fields, everything. It will be like a gravely ill person wastes away. VerseEnd Verse19 What’s left of his forest will be so small that a little boy can count them all. VerseEnd

Verse20 When that happens the remnant of Israel and survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer fear those who struck them down, but will truly trust in the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. VerseEnd Verse21 A remnant will return, a remnant of Jacob will return to the Mighty God. VerseEnd Verse22 Even though Israel’s people are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. The destruction decreed is overwhelming and righteous. VerseEnd Verse23 The Lord God of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land. VerseEnd

Verse24 Therefore the Lord God of Hosts tells 2PP you: My people who live in Zion, don’t fear the Assyrians who beat 2PP you with a club and capture 2PP you like Egypt once did. VerseEnd Verse25 Very soon My anger with 2PP you will end and I’ll impose destruction upon them. VerseEnd Verse26 The Lord of Hosts will horsewhip them like He struck down Midian at the rock of Oreb; and He’ll raise His staff to part the waters, as He did in Egypt. VerseEnd Verse27 And at that time the burden will be removed from 2PP your shoulders, and their chains taken off 2PP your neck, because of the anointing. VerseEnd

Verse28 They enter Aiath, they pass through Migron; they store supplies at Michmash. VerseEnd Verse29 They go through the pass, and they plan to camp overnight at Geba. Ramath is afraid, and Gibeah of Saul runs in fear. VerseEnd Verse30 Shout out daughter of Gallim; listen Laish! Poor Anathot! VerseEnd Verse31 Madmenah is running in fear; take cover people of Gebim! VerseEnd Verse32 They will be stopped at Nob that day; they’ll shake their fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse33 Just watch as the Lord, the Lord Almighty chops down the mighty branches with power, and the tall trees will be cut down, and the arrogant will be humbled. VerseEnd Verse34 He’ll cut down the thick forests with an ax, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One. VerseEnd

LEChapter21 Verse1 A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse, and from his roots a Branch will produce fruit. VerseEnd Verse2 The Spirit of the Lord will rest upon Him — the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of respect for the Lord — VerseEnd Verse3 and He’ll have insight and love for the Lord. He won’t judge by what He sees with His eyes, nor decide by what He hears with His ears, VerseEnd Verse4 but with righteousness He’ll judge the needy, and with justice decide matters for the poor. He’ll control the earth with words from His mouth, and with His breath He’ll slay the wicked. VerseEnd Verse5 And righteousness will be His belt, and faithfulness the sash around His waist. VerseEnd Verse6 Wolves will live beside lambs, leopards will lie beside goats; and the calf, young lion, and yearling together, and a little child will lead them. VerseEnd Verse7 And the cow will eat beside the bear, their young will lie down to rest together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox. VerseEnd Verse8 The infant will play at the cobra’s den, and a young child will put his hand in the viper’s nest. VerseEnd Verse9 They’ll neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain, because the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord like the waters cover the sea. VerseEnd

Verse10 In that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the people; the Gentiles will rally to Him, and His peace will be glorious. VerseEnd Verse11 On that day the Lord will reach out His hand a second time to reclaim the remaining remnant of His people from Assyria — also from Lower and Upper Egypt, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. VerseEnd Verse12 He’ll set up a banner for the Gentiles, and will gather the lost people of Israel, and assemble the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth. VerseEnd Verse13 All the outcasts of Israel will be gathered to His house, and the jealousy of Ephraim and Judah will end; Ephraim won’t envy Judah and Judah won’t provoke Ephraim. VerseEnd Verse14 They’ll pounce upon the shoulders of the Philistines to the west, together they’ll take the wealth of the east, they’ll subdue Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will obey them. VerseEnd Verse15 The Lord will dry up the gulf of the Egyptian Sea, and dry up the Euphrates River to let His returning people step over the remaining seven brooks. VerseEnd Verse16 There will be a highway for the returning remnant of His people from Assyria, as there had been earlier when Israel departed from Egypt. VerseEnd

LEChapter22 Verse1 And on that day, people will proclaim: Give praise to the Lord; although 2PSI You were angry with me, 2PSI Your anger has turned away and 2PSI You’ve comforted me. VerseEnd Verse2 God is my Savior. I’ll trust and not fear, for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my defense; He provided my salvation. VerseEnd Verse3 2PP You’ll joyfully draw water from the wells of salvation. VerseEnd Verse4 And on that day 2PP you’ll say: Give praise to the Lord, proclaim His name, testify about the great things He’s done for His people. VerseEnd Verse5 Sing hymns to the Lord, for He’s done glorious things; let it be known throughout the world. VerseEnd Verse6 Shout joyfully and sing, people of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel dwells among 2PP you. VerseEnd
